unrecoverable: The exact y of the alternate top-right timer: HUD.draw computes window.height - PyInt_FromLong(<runtime C value>) at hud.pyd:0x1009579b. The value is produced by earlier C-level arithmetic (most likely minimap-derived), and I did not trace it to a literal. Only the centre-clock y (window.height - 48) is a hard constant.

The clamp() bounds in draw_healthbar hud.pyx line 1059 and draw_jetpack_hud line 912 are loaded with bare fldz/fld1 forms whose operands I did not decode; 0.0 and 1.0 are the overwhelmingly likely pair given the ratio semantics, but I am not citing them as decompiled.

The default value of draw_timer's draw_bg parameter. HUD.draw's centre-clock call omits it, so the timer_frame is not drawn there, but I did not read the __defaults__ tuple to confirm the default is False.

Which of the two draw_tools_hud locals at hud.pyx lines 809/810 is bound to the 'x' parameter and which to 'ammo_x'. The stack slots shift between the assignment and the call. I assigned ammo_x = window.width-80 and x = window.width-156.5 because that makes the scaled 115x1.3 frame's centre land on width-81.75 (within 2 px of ammo_x) and its right edge 7 px from the window edge; the reverse assignment would place the panel off-screen. This is an inference, not a decompile.

The precise per-team head-icon translate offsets inside HeadCount.draw. I recovered the operand chain (HC_TEXT_WIDTH + window.width*0.5 + 10 for the left team, +10 for the right) but not the full expression grouping, so I have not stated exact icon pixel positions.

The base x term of the HP-number glTranslatef at draw_healthbar hud.pyx line 1086 — I read the '+ health_bar.width*0.23 + health_bar.anchor_x' tail and the literal 35.0, but did not confirm whether the base is the raw centre x or the already-offset bar origin.

'team.color' on the Team object (used for the health bar tint and the HeadCount text/icon tint) lives outside hud.pyd, in the game/world module. I have shown it is used verbatim as an RGB triple with 255 appended, and TEAM_COLOURS gives (44,117,179)/(137,179,44), but I did not decompile the assignment that populates Team.color to prove it is literally TEAM_COLOURS[team.id].

claims.claim:
Corrected claim: The in-game HUD is laid out in raw window pixels while the frontend menus are laid out on an 800x600 design canvas — but the mechanism is the projection matrix, not the image load scale.

- In-game: GameScene.draw sets glOrtho(0, window.width, 0, window.height, -1, 1) (gameScene.pyd 0x1013F83F, args at 0x1013F86D/0x1013F898) and never calls glScalef; HUD.draw (hud.pyd sub_1009EE80) reads `window` once at 0x1009F023 and then window.width/window.height (9 and 12 reads) combined with fixed pixel constants (MSG_LEFT_MARGIN, MSG_PAD, COLOR_PALETTE_*_PADDING_*, ammo_x). Same glOrtho form in aoslib/scenes/__init__.py:50-61.
- Menus: aoslib/scenes/frontend/menuScene.py:137-140 uses `self.manager.get_aspect(800, 600)` plus `glScalef(ratio, ratio, 1.0)`; shared/hud_constants.py:18-19 UI_SCREEN_WIDTH/HEIGHT = 800/600.
- `global_scale = 0.64` (images.py:60, re-set at :529) is an art-downsample multiplier applied to texture dimensions at load (image.py:100-101), NOT a canvas factor, and it is used on both menu and in-game art.
- Load scales are per-asset, not per-surface. load_ui's default is scale=0.6 (images.py:34). Most core HUD frames are scale=1.0 (images.py:434-435, 437-452), but weapon_frame_selected is 0.7 (images.py:436) and blueprint_background / pf_blueprint_bg_default / gdata_blueprint_bg_default are global_scale (images.py:433, 506, 514). claims.reason:
The architectural thesis survives, but both absolute quantifiers in the claim are false against primary sources, and the claim conflates two unrelated mechanisms.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (decompiled, not inferred):
1. The in-game HUD really does render in raw window pixels. In G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/aoslib/scenes/main/gameScene.pyd, GameScene.draw (sub_10138B70) fetches the module global `window` exactly once at 0x10138B73, then calls glOrtho (global fetched at 0x1013F83F) whose args are `width` at 0x1013F86D and `height` at 0x1013F898 — i.e. glOrtho(0, window.width, 0, window.height, -1, 1). It then calls `self.hud` (0x10140808) `.draw` (0x10140838) under that matrix. GameScene.draw contains NO glScalef fetch anywhere in its 0x80B8 bytes, and gameScene.pyd's string table contains no `get_aspect`.
2. Corroborated by shipped source: aoslib/scenes/__init__.py:50-56 `set_resizing_perspective` → `gl.glOrtho(0, width, 0, height, -1, 1)` with `set_normal_perspective` (lines 59-61) passing `window.width, window.height`.
3. The menu/frontend contrast is real, but it comes from a DIFFERENT mechanism than the claim says: aoslib/scenes/frontend/menuScene.py:137-140 does `x, y, width, height, ratio = self.manager.get_aspect(800, 600)` then `glScalef(ratio, ratio, 1.0)`. That, not `global_scale`, is the 800x600 design canvas. shared/hud_constants.py:18-19 also defines UI_SCREEN_WIDTH = 800 / UI_SCREEN_HEIGHT = 600, used only by menu constants (lines 141, 157-158).
4. HUD.draw itself (hud.pyd; PyMethodDef at 0x10105048 → wrapper 0x100F2A40 → body sub_1009EE80) fetches the name `window` (strtab 0x10111AE0) exactly once, at 0x1009F023, and then reads `width` (0x10112194) 9 times and `height` (0x101121DC) 12 times with no intervening receiver getattr — so they are `window.width`/`window.height` off a local. Those are mixed with hard pixel constants: MSG_LEFT_MARGIN (0x100A360D, 0x100A37F2), MSG_PAD (0x100A3BED, 0x100A4330), COLOR_PALETTE_RIGHT/BOTTOM_PADDING_UGC/DEFAULT (0x100A4C8D…0x100A4E45), `ammo_x` (0x100A0020). `global_scale` (strtab 0x10110AD4) is never fetched inside HUD.draw; its only uses in hud.pyd are in sub_100E3B30, which is the level-screenshot/UGC path (0x100E4697, 0x100E4786, 0x100E4870, adjacent to `level_screenshots/`, `map_name`, `load_ui`).

WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED:
A. "all HUD frames are loaded with scale=1.0" is FALSE, and the counterexample is inside the cited line range: images.py:436 `self.weapon_frame_selected = load_ui(..., ['weapon_select','weapon_frame_selected'], center=True, scale=0.7)`. Further in-game HUD art at non-1.0: images.py:433 `blueprint_background ... scale=global_scale`; images.py:506 `pf_blueprint_bg_default ... scale=global_scale`; images.py:514 `gdata_blueprint_bg_default ... scale=global_scale`. In-game class icons/images and score icons (images.py:~380-431) are all `scale=global_scale` too.
B. "menu art uses global_scale = 0.64" is FALSE as a rule. The main-menu frames pass no scale at all and therefore take load_ui's default: images.py:34 `def load_ui(old_tex, name, center=False, scale=0.6, ...)` — so images.py:184-189 (splash_image, main_image, main_menu_frame, name_frame, frame_3button_menu, frame_nav_bar_small) load at 0.6, not 0.64. And plenty of menu art is scale=1.0: images.py:469-472 (leaderboard_icon, options_icon, achievements_icon, tutorial_icon). Repo-wide the file has 67 `scale=1.0` and 162 `scale=global_scale` call sites — it is not a HUD-vs-menu split.
C. Mechanism conflation. `global_scale` is not a layout canvas at all: image.py:100-101 does `tex.width = int(tex.width * scale); tex.height = int(tex.height * scale)`, i.e. it is a fixed art-downsample factor baked into the texture's reported size at load. It has nothing to do with the 800x600 canvas, which is produced by menuScene's get_aspect + glScalef. Citing images.py:60 vs images.py:434-452 as the evidence for "raw pixels vs 800x600 canvas" is the wrong evidence for the right conclusion.

Note: images.py:60 `self.global_scale = 0.64` is correctly cited, but the same assignment is repeated at images.py:529 in `clear()`.

claims.reason:
Two of three components check out; the third ("unfiltered") is a misreading of the API and is wrong.

CONFIRMED (font + size). G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/aoslib/text.py:315 reads `score_hud_font = load_font(ALDO_FONT, 26, False)` and text.py:11 reads `ALDO_FONT = 'Spades'`. I did not trust the uncompyle6 output alone — I marshal-loaded aoslib/text.pyc under C:/Python27 and disassembled `set_fonts`; at bytecode offsets 768-783 for source line 315: LOAD_GLOBAL load_font / LOAD_GLOBAL ALDO_FONT / LOAD_CONST 11 (26) / LOAD_GLOBAL False / CALL_FUNCTION 3 / STORE_GLOBAL score_hud_font. It is the only assignment to score_hud_font in the tree (only other hits are text.py:82 `= None` and text.py:228 `global`), so there is no aliased second block overriding it. G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/fonts/Spades.ttf exists. score_hud_font is genuinely a HUD symbol — the byte string appears in aoslib/hud/hud.pyd, aoslib/hud.hud.pyd and aoslib/hud/hud_old.pyd.

REFUTED ("unfiltered"). The third positional argument is not a filtering flag. text.py:141 defines `def load_font(name, size, enable_resize=True)` and text.py:148 passes it as the 4th ctor arg: `Font(os.path.join(FONTS_DIRECTORY, name + '.ttf'), size, name, enable_resize)`. In font.pyd it lands on the Font attribute `enable_resize`, stored as a double at instance offset +48 — see the getter at 0x1000ABB0 (`aoslib.font.Font.enable_resize.__get__`, returns PyFloat_FromDouble(*(double *)(a1 + 48))). Its sole consumer is `aoslib.font.Font.resize_font` at 0x100141C0, which opens with `if (0.0 == *(double *)(a1 + 48))` and immediately returns the tuple (Py_ZeroStruct, 1.0) — i.e. resize disabled, scale forced to 1.0. The non-zero path divides two globals (PyNumber_Divide on dword_100964CC[dword_10096458] / dword_100964CC[dword_100963F4]), compares that ratio, and walks the font size up/down to derive a resolution-dependent pixel size and self.scale. That is DPI/resolution auto-scaling, not texture sampling. Corroborating: font.pyd's string table contains set_scale, global_font_scale, GLOBAL_FONT_SCALE, scale_fix, resize_font, get_font_scale, enable_resize — and zero occurrences of GL_LINEAR, GL_NEAREST, or any filter/mipmap/antialias token (I grepped all printable strings and ran a listing search for GL_LINEAR: 0 hits). Nothing in the retail sources touches a filter mode for fonts.

This matters for the port: reading "unfiltered" as nearest-neighbour texture sampling would produce a visibly wrong HUD score number, while the actual retail behaviour is "do not rescale this font with window resolution".

Secondary caveat, not the basis for the refutal: calling 26 "px" is unverified. text.py:114-138 `generate_font_maps` loops `for i in xrange(4, 120)` constructing `Font(..., i, ...)` and prints `font.get_char_height()` as the 'pixel_size' — i.e. the retail code itself treats the size argument as distinct from the resulting pixel height. FreeType is statically linked into font.pyd with symbols stripped (no Set_Char_Size / Set_Pixel_Sizes to resolve), so I cannot say from a primary source whether 26 is points or pixels. Treat 26 as the size argument, not a measured glyph height.

Also worth knowing: ALDO_FONT is not unconditionally 'Spades'. aoslib/strings/__init__.py:43 sets `text.ALDO_FONT = 'Edo'` for Turkish (and :39 re-affirms 'Spades' for Russian/Polish) before calling `text.set_fonts()` on the next line, so under a Turkish locale score_hud_font is Edo at 26. For English the claim's 'Spades' is right.

REFUTED on the unit (and on the line number and the "HUD" framing); the font family and the numeral 26 are correct.

1) Font family confirmed: ALDO_FONT = 'Spades' at G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/aoslib/text.py:11; G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/fonts/Spades.ttf exists.

2) Line number wrong: the assignment is at text.py:319, not :320. Line 320 is score_feed_title_font = load_font(ALDO_FONT, 20). So the literal 26 is genuine.

3) "26 px" is WRONG - 26 is a POINT size, not a pixel size. text.py:141-149 load_font(name,size,enable_resize=True) passes size straight to Font(path,size,name,enable_resize). aoslib/font.pyd carries a compiled point->pixel lookup table: strings font_map_aldo at .data:10095384, font_map_edo at .data:10095344, font_map_standard_med at .data:1009504C, plus FONT_MIN_PT_SIZE / FONT_MAX_PT_SIZE and aoslib.font.get_font_pixel_size. The real body of get_font_pixel_size is sub_10005850 (wrapper sub_100090B0, error string at .rdata:1007AD10): it PyObject_RichCompare-dispatches on the font-name argument and returns font_map_X[size]['pixel_size']. initfont builds each entry as PyFloat_FromDouble(dbl_*) stored under key dword_10096540 ('pixel_size') - see the block at 0x100164DB-0x10016513 (fld dbl_1007C790; PyFloat_FromDouble; PyDict_SetItem subdict; PyDict_SetItem outer), repeating on a 0xC0 stride through 0x10017DC9.

I resolved the value empirically from the retail binary rather than guessing: C:/Python27 is 64-bit and rejects the x86 .pyd ("DLL load failed: %1 is not a valid Win32 application"), so I used the 32-bit interpreter C:/Python27_32/py2.exe with imp.load_dynamic('font','aoslib/font.pyd'):
  font_map_aldo[26] -> {'pixel_size': 29.0087890625}
  font_map_aldo[25] -> 27.8930664062, font_map_aldo[27] -> 30.1245117188
  Font('fonts/Spades.ttf', 26, 'Spades', True).get_char_height() -> 29.0087890625
  FONT_MIN_PT_SIZE=4, FONT_MAX_PT_SIZE=119, GLOBAL_FONT_SCALE=1.0
This matches text.py:114-137 generate_font_maps, which prints 'pixel_size': font.get_char_height() for each i in xrange(4,120) - i.e. the source itself treats the constructor arg and the pixel size as different quantities. A port that sets hc_font to 26 px renders ~10% short of retail.

4) Framing wrong: hc_font is not an in-game HUD font. Its only consumers in the shipped tree are aoslib/scenes/frontend/panelBase.py:7 and :81 (default font= for panel draw_text) and aoslib/scenes/ingame_menus/loadingMenu.py:9. The actual HUD fonts (ammo_font_hud text.py:299, reserve_font :300, score_hud_font :315) are constructed with enable_resize=False; hc_font takes the default True, so it is additionally subject to runtime rescaling (Font.resize_font / Font.scale / GLOBAL_FONT_SCALE, all exported by font.pyd).

INFERENCE (labelled): the claim's author most likely read the size argument as pixels because the name "size" is ambiguous; I did not find any source in the retail tree that states hc_font is 26 pixels.

In font.pyd the attribute is aoslib.font.Font.enable_resize (property code objects at 0x1007ADB4 / 0x1007ADDC) and what it gates is aoslib.font.Font.resize_font (name string 0x1007B520, body sub_100141C0), which divides two screen-dimension globals by two base-dimension globals (PyNumber_Divide at 0x10014324 and 0x100143C1), min-selects the ratio (PyObject_RichCompare op 0 at 0x10014407), then steps the nominal size up/down one at a time (PyNumber_InPlaceAdd 0x10014B28 / PyNumber_InPlaceSubtract 0x10015002) re-instantiating the face until it fits, and stores a scale at 0x10015372. Porting False as "nearest-neighbour / unfiltered atlas" would implement the wrong thing and silently drop the actual DPI behaviour.

I did not recover the exact FT_Set_Char_Size/FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes call or DPI used, so the exact rendered pixel height for size 26 is unrecovered; I am not inventing one.

claims.original: png/ui/jetpack_fuel/jetpack_fuel_bar.png is a 33x130 vertical gradient that runs from pale yellow at the top to saturated red at the bottom, and jetpack_fuel_frame.png is the matching 33x130 surround.
claims.reason: Partially refuted — the bar half is confirmed, the frame half is wrong. CONFIRMED by direct pixel inspection of G:/AoSRevival/aceofspades_source/png/ui/jetpack_fuel/jetpack_fuel_bar.png: raw PNG IHDR gives width=33 height=130 bitdepth=8 colortype=6, and the image is a vertical gradient with R constant at 255 and G,B both strictly monotone decreasing top->bottom (topmost opaque row y=10 = (255,251,217) pale cream-yellow; bottommost row y=119 = (255,1,0) saturated red); every interior row is horizontally flat. REFUTED: jetpack_fuel_frame.png is 33x130 (IHDR confirmed) but is NOT a "surround". Its interior is solid opaque black — sampling x=10..23, y=20..99 yields (0,0,0,255) for all 1120 pixels; the whole image is 2623 pure-black pixels plus a dark-olive (43,37,3) border, and 93.9% of it is opaque (alpha>200). A surround/outline would be hollow so the bar reads through; this is a filled black backing plate that must be drawn UNDER the bar or it completely occludes it — an error that changes draw order at port time. Additionally the gradient does not fill its canvas: the bar's alpha bbox is (4, 9, 28, 120), i.e. the visible gradient is 24 wide x 111 tall inset in the 33x130 sheet, so a fuel fill-fraction crop taken against the full 130px height is off by 19px. Provenance is also mislabelled: "STATED AS: decompiled" is inaccurate — no decompilation supports any of this, it is asset inspection only. No competing copies of either file exist anywhere in the retail tree (recursive search for jetpack_fuel* returned only these two files plus jetpack_icon.png).
